name: Charismatic Conqueror
oracle_text:
Vigilance
Whenever an artifact or creature an opponent controls enters untapped, they may tap that permanent. If they don't, you create a 1/1 white Vampire creature token with lifelink.
blocked_sentences: Whenever an artifact or creature an opponent controls enters untapped, they may tap that permanent. If they don't, you create a 1/1 white Vampire creature token with lifelink.

needs.what: a way for a `permanent_enters` trigger to match only on the permanent's tapped state *as it arrives*, checked once when the ability queues and never again -- either by having `matches_card_filter` honour the `tapped` key it already accepts and then discards, or by putting the arrival's tapped state on the ENTERS_BATTLEFIELD event and adding it to `EVENT_BINDING_KEYS` so a filter clause can read it
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Two near misses, both wrong. (1) `filter: {"tapped": false}` LOADS and does nothing: `loader` validates a trigger filter with `validate_selector` against `SELECTOR_KEYS`, which contains `tapped`, but `triggers.matches_card_filter` reads controller, zone, types, subtypes, supertypes, colors, keywords, is_token, is_commander, mana_value, power and toughness and never looks at `tapped` at all. The clause is silently dropped, so the card would also trigger on every artifact and creature an opponent plays *tapped* -- strictly wider than the printed line, and wider is the dangerous direction the surrounding comments in that same function call out. (2) The trigger's `condition`, `{"exists": {"binding": "subject", "tapped": false}}`, does read the state correctly at queue time (`zones.enter_battlefield` sets `obj.tapped` before it fires the event, and `selectors.matches` honours `tapped`) but it makes the clause an intervening-if, and `stack.py` re-evaluates a trigger's `condition` on resolution per 603.4. This card's own printed ruling is the opposite: if the permanent is tapped by the time the ability resolves, its controller cannot tap it, so you DO create the token. Under the condition spelling the ability instead resolves as `skipped="condition"` and makes nothing -- and that is not a corner case, it is the line an opponent takes by simply tapping the freshly-arrived artifact for mana in response. There is no third spelling: no condition key, value key or event binding reports how a permanent arrived, and moving the check into the ability's effects as an `if` asks it at resolution rather than at arrival, which is wrong in both directions at once.
